clips.send: Pacing. How fast the story moves. Summarizing a long span or skipping ahead speeds it up. Showing a scene in detail slows it down. Three weeks passed. Then, on the last night, every second stretched like an hour. Effect: Slow pacing at the climax builds tension; fast pacing skips the boring parts.

clips.send: The Sound in the Attic. The week we moved into the old house on Birch Street, it rained every single afternoon. Mom said the place just needed “a little attention,” but my little brother refused to go upstairs alone. On the first night, I noticed that the chipped bowl someone had left on the back porch was licked clean, and we didn’t have a pet. Thunder rolled over the hills while I did my homework at the kitchen table. Around midnight, something above my ceiling went scritch, scritch, scritch, and then stopped. The next morning, our neighbor leaned over the fence. “The last family never did fix that torn screen on the attic window,” he said. I told myself it was just the wind. That afternoon, a trail of tiny paw prints crossed the dust on the attic stairs. We ate pizza off moving boxes because the table was still buried under bubble wrap. At bedtime my brother swore he heard “a baby crying” inside the wall. On Saturday, I finally climbed the attic ladder with a flashlight, my heart pounding in my ears.

clips.send: Point of view. The perspective a story is told from. Common choices are first person (“I”), third-person limited and third-person omniscient. First person: I never told anyone what I saw that night. Effect: Controls what readers know — a first-person narrator can hide things, which creates suspense.

clips.send: The Sound in the Attic. The week we moved into the old house on Birch Street, it rained every single afternoon. Mom said the place just needed “a little attention,” but my little brother refused to go upstairs alone. On the first night, I noticed that the chipped bowl someone had left on the back porch was licked clean, and we didn’t have a pet. Thunder rolled over the hills while I did my homework at the kitchen table. Around midnight, something above my ceiling went scritch, scritch, scritch, and then stopped. The next morning, our neighbor leaned over the fence. “The last family never did fix that torn screen on the attic window,” he said. I told myself it was just the wind. That afternoon, a trail of tiny paw prints crossed the dust on the attic stairs. We ate pizza off moving boxes because the table was still buried under bubble wrap. At bedtime my brother swore he heard “a baby crying” inside the wall. On Saturday, I finally climbed the attic ladder with a flashlight, my heart pounding in my ears. The beam swept across old trunks and landed on a pile of sweaters in the corner. Two green eyes blinked back at me. A thin gray cat lifted her head, and from behind her tumbled four tiny kittens, mewing like, well, like a baby crying. She had been slipping in through the torn screen every night, scratching around up there, and eating from the porch bowl. My brother named her Scritch.

clips.send: In medias res. Latin for “in the middle of things.” The story opens with the action already underway. It may fill in earlier events later. Early in Homer’s Odyssey, Odysseus is stranded on an island, years after the Trojan War. Later, he tells the story of his earlier adventures. Effect: A strong hook: readers are thrown into action and keep reading to understand it.

clips.send: 叙述视角。讲故事时采用的视角。常见的有第一人称（“我”）、第三人称有限视角和第三人称全知视角。 第一人称：那天晚上看到的事，我从来没告诉过任何人。 作用：决定读者知道多少——第一人称叙述者可以隐瞒信息，从而制造悬念。

clips.send: 阁楼里的声音。搬进桦树街那栋老房子的那个星期，每天下午都下雨。妈妈说，这房子“稍微收拾一下就好”，可弟弟说什么也不肯一个人上楼。第一天晚上，我发现后门廊上那只缺了口的旧碗被舔得干干净净——可我们家根本没养宠物。我在厨房的桌子上写作业，群山间传来隆隆雷声。半夜，天花板上面传来“嚓、嚓、嚓”三声，然后就没动静了。第二天早上，隔壁邻居隔着篱笆探过身来说：“上一家人一直没修阁楼窗户上那块破纱窗。”我对自己说，那只是风。那天下午，阁楼楼梯的灰尘上出现了一串小小的爪印。桌子还埋在一堆气泡膜底下，我们只好把披萨放在搬家纸箱上吃。睡觉前，弟弟发誓说他听见墙里面有“小宝宝在哭”。星期六，我终于拿着手电筒爬上了阁楼的梯子，心跳声咚咚地响在耳朵里。

clips.send: 阁楼里的声音。搬进桦树街那栋老房子的那个星期，每天下午都下雨。妈妈说，这房子“稍微收拾一下就好”，可弟弟说什么也不肯一个人上楼。第一天晚上，我发现后门廊上那只缺了口的旧碗被舔得干干净净——可我们家根本没养宠物。我在厨房的桌子上写作业，群山间传来隆隆雷声。半夜，天花板上面传来“嚓、嚓、嚓”三声，然后就没动静了。第二天早上，隔壁邻居隔着篱笆探过身来说：“上一家人一直没修阁楼窗户上那块破纱窗。”我对自己说，那只是风。那天下午，阁楼楼梯的灰尘上出现了一串小小的爪印。桌子还埋在一堆气泡膜底下，我们只好把披萨放在搬家纸箱上吃。睡觉前，弟弟发誓说他听见墙里面有“小宝宝在哭”。星期六，我终于拿着手电筒爬上了阁楼的梯子，心跳声咚咚地响在耳朵里。 手电筒的光扫过几只旧箱子，落在角落里一堆旧毛衣上。一双绿眼睛眨了眨，正看着我。一只瘦瘦的灰猫抬起头，四只小奶猫从它身后跌跌撞撞地钻出来，细细地叫着，听起来真像婴儿在哭。原来，它每天夜里都从那块破纱窗钻进来，在阁楼里窸窸窣窣地走动，再溜到门廊上吃碗里的东西。弟弟给它取名叫“嚓嚓”。
